prompt:
Return a single bare JSON object with exactly these five keys: name, phone, email, company, country. Every value must be a string or JSON null. No prose, Markdown, extra keys, or omitted keys.

1. Read the record only. The user supplies a short note containing one contact block of label–value lines. Recognize variant labels and separators (colon, equals, tab), including shuffled lines. Ignore surrounding text and signatures. Trim each value and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space. Mark absent lines, blank values and whole-value placeholders (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD, any case) as missing.

2. Assign raw values. The country value comes from its own line when present. For the other lines, a value containing @ belongs to email, and a value with at least seven digits and only digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after removing leading tel: and an extension belongs to phone, regardless of label. Extensions are trailing ext. N, ext N, xN, #N or extension N, with numeric N. For name and company, use the labeled values unless the name line ends in a legal suffix and the company line does not; then swap the values before doing any cleanup. Legal suffix list, case-insensitive: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

3. Resolve the country and phone together. Map a supplied country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, all case-insensitive, and common aliases (UK and Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA and U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ). Strip tel: and the extension from the phone. Check for + or 00 at the start, ignoring an opening parenthesis. If international, remove (0), then remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and replace leading 00 with +. Keep the calling code as written. Do not alter a supplied country to match that code or alter the code to match the country. If the country line is missing, blank, or a placeholder, fill country from the international calling code only when it uniquely identifies a country. Shared codes such as +1 or +7 leave country null. This is the only exception to missing values staying null. If national, remove formatting and one leading trunk 0 if present, then prepend + and the resolved country's calling code. A national phone without a country is null. A phone string is E.164: a plus followed by digits only.

4. Clean the remaining values. Name: split Last, First at the first comma and reorder to First Last; remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, case-insensitively, with or without a dot; uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Company: remove the trailing legal suffix and optional preceding comma, trim, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics through case changes; never transliterate. Email: remove surrounding angle brackets and any mailto: prefix and lowercase the entire address.

5. Emit all five keys. Missing fields are null, not empty strings. Do not guess or use notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes as sources for missing fields.
